answer: Sealed spec written to untracked/races/A-spec/sonnet/spec.md for T936 (run 4x4.D3 to completion). Six decisions made and not deferred: (1) node cap stays 20,000,000/root, unchanged from T924/T929/T930/T932, so the run stays comparable; raising or dropping it was considered and rejected. (2) a censored root's table slot stays UNDEF (already the shipped behavior, no code change) and the write-up must report closed/censored/total as three separate numbers, never one blended mean -- the exact defect T929 corrected in T924's doc, one level downstream. (3) three controls specified concretely: null (4x3 byte-identical node/orbit counts, speedup >= 10.5x, 10% margin under T932's measured 11.64x), seeded-defect (round-robin vs RETRO_PARTITION=contig, 1.40 max/mean threshold reused from tools/regression-finishparallel-partition.sh but run at the 4x3 rung itself, not the 3x3 CI proxy), and killed-run (kill -INT only -- verified from src/retro.zig:2184-2190 that installParallelSigint registers SIG.INT alone, so SIGTERM/SIGKILL do NOT trigger the checkpoint save; this is stated as the run's one operating rule). (4) the run must be a sequence of 4h segments each closed by a deliberate SIGINT, because finishParallel checkpoints only once per segment (at interrupt or completion, never during) -- a hard crash mid-segment loses that segment's work with no code change able to prevent it at this scope; hard stop at 240h cumulative segment wall (~1-9x T930's 1-6 day estimate and T929's 26.8-214.7h lower bound) closes the row blocked with the partial checkpoint. (5) what every segment must record, keyed to fields tools/goban-scaling-capture.sh (T926) already emits (tree-walked peak RSS, killed_by, partial, regime_observed) plus per-thread imbalance and checkpoint file identity. (6) detached at two levels -- job_start wraps a segmenting shell loop, which wraps goban-scaling-capture.sh, which wraps the retro binary; no agent holds any wall, matching T928's stated boundary. Ten acceptance arms (armed count 10), each a red-then-green must with the incident it would have caught. One correction to the brief's own framing, checked against source: RETRO_4X4=1 is documented in retro.zig's header comment (line 3246) but never read by runParallel -- 4x4 is the default when RETRO_3X3 and RETRO_4X3 are both unset -- given its own acceptance arm (Arm 0) because a copy-pasted 4x3 control command carrying RETRO_4X3=1 forward would silently re-run 4x3 and look like a 4x4-shaped early exit. Out-of-scope list includes: no code change to src/retro.zig, Track B at 4x4, raising/removing the cap (decided against, not deferred), a daemon/watchdog for the loop, and automating the blocked write-up judgement.
notes: Numbers checked against docs/research/4x4-d3-tractability.md, 4x4-d3-weighted-projection.md, parallel-finisher-cost.md and findings/T932-finishparallel-roundrobin.json -- all four matched the brief's table with no discrepancy. Read src/retro.zig directly (worker/finishParallel/parallelBoard/runParallel/installParallelSigint, lines ~1330-1723 and ~3200-3461) rather than trusting any doc's description of the mechanism, which is where the SIGINT-only finding and the RETRO_4X4 dead-flag finding came from. Read tools/goban-scaling-capture.sh and its T926 findings file to reuse the existing kill/RSS/regime-observation instrument instead of re-specifying one. Read docs/infra/host/detached-jobs.md (T928), docs/infra/host/ram-policy.md (T806) and docs/infra/host/macos-timeout-gap.md to ground the segmenting-loop design in a signal-based kill/wait rather than macOS's absent timeout(1). Did not run any solve, per the brief's Build nothing / Run no solve instruction. Inbox checked twice (start and pre-done), both times empty.
